*Comprehensive market data showing how AI-powered and no-code platforms are reshaping the economics of building web and mobile applications*


The mobile app development market is undergoing a significant shift. Traditional development costs can create substantial barriers for non-technical founders and small businesses. According to Clutch's pricing guide, mobile app development projects reviewed on its platform typically[cost $10,000 to $49,999](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) , while the average reported project cost is approximately $90,780. Meanwhile, platforms like Floot enable builders to create full-stack web and mobile applications[through conversational AI](https://floot.com/) , offering an alternative for entrepreneurs who need to validate ideas quickly.


The numbers tell a compelling story: low-code and no-code platforms can reduce initial development expenses in some use cases compared to traditional development, while AI-assisted development can reduce costs and shorten timelines for certain tasks. These statistics reveal where the market stands, how development costs vary, and what builders should consider when planning applications in 2027.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Floot makes full-stack app development more accessible** : Its MCP connector lets users build applications[through Claude or ChatGPT](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) while Floot manages hosting, databases, authentication, and deployment
- **Traditional development remains expensive** : Clutch reports an average mobile app development project cost of[approximately $90,780](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) , although individual project costs vary considerably
- **Low-code platforms show significant market growth** : The global low-code market was[estimated at $44.6 billion](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) for 2026 and is projected to reach $101.7 billion by 2030
- **AI can accelerate development work** : A GitHub study found developers completed a specific coding task[55% faster](https://github.blog/news-insights/research/research-quantifying-github-copilots-impact-on-developer-productivity-and-happiness/) using GitHub Copilot
- **Maintenance adds ongoing costs** : A 2024 research study notes that software maintenance can account for[up to 70%](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11419633/) of total software development life-cycle costs


## **Understanding the Core Components of App Development Costs**


Before diving into specific numbers, it is essential to understand what drives app development costs. The total investment includes planning, design, development, testing, deployment, and ongoing maintenance. Each component contributes to the final price tag, and understanding these factors helps builders make informed decisions about their approach.


### **1. Mobile app development projects typically cost $10,000 to $49,999 on Clutch**


According to Clutch's pricing guide, mobile app development projects reviewed on its platform typically cost[between $10,000 and $49,999](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) . This range reflects reported projects rather than a universal development price. Applications with advanced features, complex integrations, custom user interfaces, and extensive backend requirements can cost substantially more. The final investment depends on project scope, developer experience, and technical requirements.


### **2. The average app development project cost is approximately $90,780**


According to Clutch's 2026 pricing guide, the average reported mobile app development project[cost is $90,780.11](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) . Actual project costs vary substantially by scope and complexity. Features, user interface requirements, backend architecture, and development timelines all influence the total investment. This average reflects projects reported through Clutch and should not be treated as the standard price for every mobile application.


### **3. Mobile app development companies commonly charge between $25 and $49 per hour**


Clutch's pricing data indicates that mobile app development companies commonly charge[between $25 and $49](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) per hour. Rates vary by region, development experience, and project requirements. More specialized services may carry higher rates. Hourly pricing is only one part of the cost calculation because complex applications can require substantial time for development, testing, integrations, and revisions.


## **Decoding Development Time and Its Impact on Project Budgets**


Time directly translates to money in app development. The longer a project takes, the more expensive it can become. Understanding how different approaches affect timelines helps builders optimize their budgets.


### **4. Mobile app development projects take approximately 11 months on average**


According to Clutch's pricing guide, the average timeline for mobile app development projects reported on its platform is[approximately 11 months](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) . Actual delivery times depend on complexity, development methodology, team capacity, and project requirements. Smaller applications may be completed sooner, while projects involving multiple platforms, integrations, and extensive testing can require longer development cycles.


### **5. Developers completed one coding task 55% faster with GitHub Copilot**


In a GitHub study involving 95 professional developers, participants using GitHub Copilot completed a specific JavaScript task[55% faster](https://github.blog/news-insights/research/research-quantifying-github-copilots-impact-on-developer-productivity-and-happiness/) than those without it. Developers using Copilot took approximately 1 hour and 11 minutes, compared with 2 hours and 41 minutes for the control group. Results for complete applications and overall project costs may differ.


### **6. A vendor reported that low-code could reduce development time by up to 90%**


Grand View Research cites a 2023 claim by Kissflow that low-code platforms can reduce application[development time by 90%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) . This is a vendor-reported figure rather than a verified industry-wide average. Actual time savings depend on application complexity, customization requirements, integrations, and the development team's experience with low-code tools.


### **7. A 2015 Standish Group study classified 29% of projects as successful**


The 2015 Standish Group CHAOS Report classified[29% of software projects](https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/chaos-report-2015/169924198) as successful under its modern resolution criteria. The report defined success as completing a project on time, within budget, and with a satisfactory result. These historical findings illustrate how difficult it can be to satisfy multiple project objectives simultaneously.


### **8. A 2015 study classified 52% of software projects as challenged**


The 2015 Standish Group CHAOS Report classified[52% of software projects](https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/chaos-report-2015/169924198) as challenged under its modern resolution criteria. These projects did not satisfy all the requirements for successful delivery. The historical results highlight the importance of managing scope, budgets, timelines, and customer expectations throughout software development rather than treating project completion as the only measure of success.


## **Platform-Specific Costs: Web, iOS, and Android Development**


Choosing the right platform strategy significantly impacts total development costs. Native development for multiple platforms can increase expenses, while cross-platform and web-based approaches may reduce duplicate development work.


### **9. A 2023 survey reported 46% usage of Flutter among surveyed developers**


According to a 2023 developer survey reported by Statista,[46% of surveyed developers](https://www.statista.com/statistics/869224/worldwide-software-developer-working-hours/) reported using Flutter, making it a prominent cross-platform framework in that survey. Cross-platform frameworks allow developers to share code between operating systems, potentially reducing duplicated work. However, actual cost savings depend on platform-specific requirements and application complexity.


### **10. Apple charges $99 per year for developer membership**


The Apple Developer Program costs[$99 per membership year](https://developer.apple.com/programs/) in the United States, with regional pricing differences possible. App Store commissions apply to qualifying digital sales, with rates depending on transaction type and program eligibility. Approved developers enrolled in Apple's Small Business Program can qualify for a[reduced 15% commission rate](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/small-business-program/) on eligible transactions.


### **11. Google Play charges a $25 registration fee with variable service fees**


Google Play requires a[one-time $25 registration fee](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6112435) for a developer account. Additional service fees apply to qualifying digital transactions, with[rates varying by region](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/112622) , purchase type, billing method, and program eligibility. Developers should also account for applicable account verification, testing, and publishing requirements before releasing an application.


### **12. Google says 97% of Play developers are not subject to service fees**


According to Google Play's guidance,[97% of developers](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11131145) are not subject to Play service fees. Fees generally apply to developers offering qualifying paid apps or digital purchases rather than automatically applying to every application. Google also states that most developers who are subject to service fees qualify for rates of 15% or less.


## **Developer Compensation and Infrastructure Expenses**


Every functional app requires development expertise and appropriate infrastructure. Understanding these costs helps builders plan beyond frontend design and account for the resources needed to operate an application.


### **13. The median US software developer salary was $135,980 in 2025**


According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the median annual wage for software developers was[$135,980 in May 2025](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/computer-and-information-technology/software-developers.htm) . This figure covers software developers broadly, not only mobile app specialists. Hiring employees also involves additional expenses such as benefits, equipment, management, and infrastructure. These costs can affect the total budget for businesses maintaining internal development teams.


## **The Low-Code and No-Code Revolution in App Development Costs**


The emergence of low-code and no-code platforms has changed the cost equation for certain types of application development. Market research, adoption surveys, and industry forecasts provide context for this shift.


### **14. The low-code market was estimated at $44.6 billion for 2026**


A Grand View Research forecast published in January 2024 estimated that the global low-code application development platform market would reach[$44.6 billion in 2026](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) . This was a market estimate, not a confirmed year-end revenue result. The forecast reflected anticipated demand for tools that simplify software development and reduce the need for extensive manual coding.


### **15. The low-code market is projected to reach $101.7 billion by 2030**


The global low-code application development platform market was[valued at $24.8 billion](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) in 2023 and was projected to grow to $101.7 billion by 2030, according to Grand View Research's January 2024 forecast. The report estimated a compound annual growth rate of 22.5% from 2024 to 2030. These figures represent a forecast rather than guaranteed future market performance.


### **16. An earlier forecast expected 80% of non-IT professionals to help develop IT products by 2024**


An earlier forecast cited by Grand View Research expected[80% of non-IT professionals](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) to develop IT products and services by 2024, with more than 65% anticipated to use low-code or no-code tools. These were projections, not verified adoption results. They illustrate the expectations surrounding citizen development at the time the forecast was made.


### **17. A survey found 70% of inexperienced low-code users learned within one month**


A Mendix survey cited by G2's research summary reported that[70% of low-code users](https://www.g2.com/articles/low-code-development-statistics) who had no previous experience learned low-code development within one month or less. The finding suggests that some low-code tools can be accessible to beginners. However, learning basic development skills does not automatically mean users can build complex, production-ready applications without additional support.


### **18. Low-code platforms accounted for over 71% of market revenue by component in 2023**


According to Grand View Research, the platform component accounted for[more than 71%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/low-code-application-development-platform-market) of the global low-code application development platform market's revenue in 2023. This indicates that platforms represented the largest component of the measured market. The statistic refers specifically to revenue distribution within the low-code market, not the percentage of all software applications built using low-code tools.


## **Project Budget and Timeline Risks**


Budget overruns and missed deadlines can increase total software project costs. Historical project outcomes provide context for understanding and managing these risks.


### **19. A historical study found 44% of projects stayed on budget**


Historical Standish Group figures covering FY2011-2015 reported that[44% of software projects](https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/chaos-report-2015/169924198) stayed on budget and 40% finished on time. The analysis covered more than 25,000 projects across the reporting period. Although these figures are historical rather than current-year estimates, they illustrate the challenges of managing software delivery within planned financial and scheduling constraints.


## **Post-Launch Maintenance and Update Costs**


The costs do not stop at launch. Ongoing maintenance and updates can represent a significant portion of total software ownership costs.


### **20. Software maintenance can account for up to 70% of life-cycle costs**


A 2024 research study published in *PeerJ Computer Science* notes that software maintenance can account for[up to 70%](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11419633/) of total software development life-cycle costs. This figure concerns the broader software life cycle rather than a standard annual maintenance fee. It illustrates why updates, bug fixes, compatibility work, and long-term application support deserve attention during initial budget planning.


### **21. A software maintenance study analyzed 1,656 maintenance requests**


The same 2024 research study analyzed[1,656 maintenance requests](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11419633/) for mobile applications. Researchers investigated automated classification methods that could help organize and process maintenance work. The findings demonstrate the range of activities involved in keeping software operational after deployment. Maintenance requirements vary with application complexity, technical dependencies, and the frequency of updates.


## **Market Growth and the Opportunity Ahead**


Understanding market trends helps builders see the opportunity in front of them. Revenue, engagement, and download statistics provide additional context for evaluating the economics of app development.


### **22. The mobile app development market reached $302.1 billion in 2025**


The global mobile app development market was[valued at $302.1 billion](https://straitsresearch.com/report/mobile-app-development-market) in 2025, according to Straits Research. The report projects growth to $844.50 billion by 2034, representing a compound annual growth rate of 12.1% during 2026-2034. These figures reflect the research firm's market definition and forecast assumptions rather than guaranteed future revenue.


### **23. Consumer spending on mobile apps reached $150 billion in 2024**


According to Sensor Tower's report, global consumer spending on mobile apps[reached $150 billion](https://sensortower.com/press/sensor-tower-consumer-spending-on-apps-soared-in-2024-and-mobile-rode-the-wave-of-ai-enthusiasm) in 2024, representing a 13% year-over-year increase. The figure includes spending on in-app purchases, subscriptions, and paid apps and games. It demonstrates the scale of mobile app monetization across major app stores, although revenue opportunities vary significantly by category.


### **24. A 2015 study estimated 37% larger transactions among certain US mobile shoppers**


A 2015 McKinsey analysis estimated that US consumers who regularly purchased products using mobile phones spent[37% more per transaction](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/growth-marketing-and-sales/our-insights/how-some-companies-are-using-mobile-to-power-growth) than those who primarily shopped online using PCs. The historical comparison reflects a specific retail consumer segment. It should not be generalized to every mobile application, business model, or customer population.


### **25. A 2020 estimate placed 88% of US adults' mobile internet time in apps**


According to eMarketer's 2020 estimates, US adults were expected to spend[approximately 88%](https://www.emarketer.com/content/the-majority-of-americans-mobile-time-spent-takes-place-in-apps/) of their mobile internet time in apps rather than browsers. This historical estimate illustrates substantial engagement with mobile applications. However, it does not mean every business needs a native mobile app, as modern websites can also deliver interactive experiences.


### **26. Mobile users spent approximately 3.6 hours daily in apps in 2025**


According to Sensor Tower's 2026 report, mobile users spent approximately[3.6 hours per day](https://sensortower.com/blog/state-of-mobile-2026) in apps in 2025. Total time spent across iOS and Google Play reached 5.3 trillion hours, increasing 3.8% year over year. These figures highlight the scale of mobile engagement while reflecting worldwide usage rather than the behavior of every individual user.


### **27. Global app downloads approached 150 billion in 2025**


According to Sensor Tower's 2026 report, downloads across iOS and Google Play reached[nearly 150 billion](https://sensortower.com/blog/state-of-mobile-2026) in 2025, increasing approximately 0.8% year over year. The figure exceeded the previous download peak recorded in 2023. The relatively modest growth rate suggests that app markets are increasingly mature, making engagement and monetization important considerations alongside new downloads.


### **28. Approximately 97% of Google Play apps are free to download**


According to 42matters store data,[approximately 97%](https://42matters.com/stats) of Google Play apps and 95% of Apple App Store apps were free to download as of August 10, 2026. These figures demonstrate how widespread free-to-download distribution models are across both stores. Applications may still generate revenue through subscriptions, advertising, in-app purchases, or other monetization methods.


## **How Floot Helps Reduce AI App Development Costs**


The statistics highlight the financial considerations involved in traditional app development. Floot offers[a different approach](https://floot.com/) for non-technical founders, operators, and small businesses. Its MCP connector works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and compatible tools to[build full-stack applications](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) while Floot handles hosting, Postgres databases, authentication, storage, and deployment.


Floot's[pricing plans](https://floot.com/pricing) provide several starting options:


- **Free** : 100 building actions per day and a one-time $3 hosting credit
- **Pro** : $25/month with 1,000 building actions per day and $10/month in hosting allowance
- **Power** : $100/month with 5,000 building actions per day and $25/month in hosting allowance
- **Mobile builds** : 2 per month on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited on Power
- **AI costs** : Connector building uses the user's existing AI subscription, while optional Floot AI features may consume separate credits


Hosting beyond included allowances is usage-based. Floot supports[mobile app publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) , but Google Play connection requires a paid Floot plan, developer accounts are still required, and store approval is not guaranteed. Builders own their code and data, while ZIP export requires a paid plan.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What are the typical cost ranges for developing a mobile app in 2027?**


Mobile app development costs vary significantly by complexity and requirements. According to Clutch's pricing guide, projects reviewed on its platform typically[cost $10,000 to $49,999](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) , while the average reported project cost is approximately $90,780. More complex projects may require larger budgets. Low-code, no-code, and AI-assisted approaches can lower upfront expenses for certain use cases. For builders seeking working[applications with managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , Floot's connector provides another option.


### **How does using AI assistance impact app development costs?**


AI assistance can reduce the time required for specific development tasks, although overall savings depend on project requirements. In a GitHub study involving 95 developers, participants using GitHub Copilot completed a specific JavaScript task[55% faster](https://github.blog/news-insights/research/research-quantifying-github-copilots-impact-on-developer-productivity-and-happiness/) than those without it. These results do not establish an equivalent reduction in complete application development costs. Testing, deployment, infrastructure, and maintenance still contribute to total expenses.


### **What ongoing costs should I anticipate after launching my app?**


Ongoing costs may include hosting, database usage, security updates, maintenance, third-party services, and app store fees. A 2024 research study notes that software maintenance can account for[up to 70%](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11419633/) of total life-cycle costs, although this is not an annual spending estimate. For applications hosted through Floot,[hosting costs](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/hosting) depend on resource usage, with monthly allowances available on paid plans. Usage beyond the allowance draws on prepaid hosting credit.


### **Can I develop a functional app on a limited budget with platforms like Floot?**


Yes. Low-code, no-code, and AI-assisted approaches can lower initial development costs, depending on project scope. Floot is[free to start](https://floot.com/pricing) with 100 building actions per day and a one-time $3 hosting credit. Pro starts at $25/month, and Power starts at $100/month. Mobile builds are available on every plan, but connecting Google Play requires a paid Floot plan. Apple and Google developer accounts are required for store publishing.


### **What factors cause the biggest cost variations in app development?**


The primary cost drivers include app complexity, platform choice, developer experience, feature requirements, and development approach. According to Clutch's pricing data, mobile app development companies commonly charge[between $25 and $49](https://clutch.co/directory/mobile-application-developers/pricing) per hour, although rates vary significantly. Native development, cross-platform frameworks, and web applications involve different technical requirements. AI-assisted and no-code approaches can lower upfront spending in some cases, but ongoing hosting, maintenance, and integration costs must still be considered.
